import HartshorneLib.Chapter4LogarithmicDifferentialResidue
import HartshorneLib.Chapter4IntrinsicResidue
import HartshorneLib.Chapter4ProductFormulaConsequences
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Finprod

/-!
# The global residue theorem for logarithmic differentials

The intrinsic residues of `dg/g` have finite support and sum to zero on a
smooth proper integral curve. This follows from the local residue-order formula
and the principal-divisor product formula. The general global residue theorem
for arbitrary rational differentials is a separate obligation.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry

namespace Hartshorne

noncomputable section

attribute [local instance] functionFieldOverAlgebra stalkOverAlgebra
  stalkFunctionFieldOver_isScalarTower

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
variable (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral X.left]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 X.hom]

/-- Nonzero logarithmic residues occur only at zeros and poles of the
function. This containment can be strict in positive characteristic. -/
theorem support_curveLogResidue_subset (g : X.left.functionFieldˣ) :
    Function.support (fun p : {x : X.left // x ≠ genericPoint X.left} =>
      curveSimplePoleResidueToBase X p.2
        ⟨curveLogDifferential X g, curveLogDifferential_mem_simplePole X p.2 g⟩) ⊆
      {p | orderZAt X.hom p.2 g ≠ 1} := by
  intro p hp horder
  apply hp
  dsimp only
  rw [curveSimplePoleResidueToBase_log_eq_order, horder]
  simp

variable [IsProper X.hom]

/-- A logarithmic differential has only finitely many nonzero residues. -/
theorem curveLogResidue_support_finite (g : X.left.functionFieldˣ) :
    (Function.support (fun p : {x : X.left // x ≠ genericPoint X.left} =>
      curveSimplePoleResidueToBase X p.2
        ⟨curveLogDifferential X g, curveLogDifferential_mem_simplePole X p.2 g⟩)).Finite :=
  (orderZAt_support_finite X.hom g).subset (support_curveLogResidue_subset X g)

/-- The sum over all closed points of the intrinsic residues of a logarithmic
differential vanishes. The preceding finite-support theorem ensures that this
is an ordinary finite sum, including in positive characteristic. -/
theorem finsum_curveLogResidue_eq_zero (g : X.left.functionFieldˣ) :
    (∑ᶠ p : {x : X.left // x ≠ genericPoint X.left},
      curveSimplePoleResidueToBase X p.2
        ⟨curveLogDifferential X g, curveLogDifferential_mem_simplePole X p.2 g⟩) = 0 := by
  classical
  rw [finsum_eq_sum_of_support_subset _ (s := (orderZAt_support_finite X.hom g).toFinset)
    (by simpa only [Set.Finite.coe_toFinset] using support_curveLogResidue_subset X g)]
  calc
    _ = (principalOrderSum (X := X) g : k) := by
      simp only [principalOrderSum, Int.cast_sum, curveSimplePoleResidueToBase_log_eq_order]
    _ = 0 := by rw [principalOrderSum_eq_zero_of_smoothProperIntegralCurve X g, Int.cast_zero]

/-- The intrinsic residue map satisfies the global residue theorem on every
logarithmic differential. -/
theorem finsum_curveRationalDifferentialResidue_log_eq_zero
    (g : X.left.functionFieldˣ) :
    (∑ᶠ p : {x : X.left // x ≠ genericPoint X.left},
      curveRationalDifferentialResidue X p.2 (curveLogDifferential X g)) = 0 := by
  calc
    _ = ∑ᶠ p : {x : X.left // x ≠ genericPoint X.left},
        curveSimplePoleResidueToBase X p.2
          ⟨curveLogDifferential X g, curveLogDifferential_mem_simplePole X p.2 g⟩ :=
      finsum_congr fun p => curveRationalDifferentialResidue_eq_simplePole X p.2
        ⟨curveLogDifferential X g, curveLogDifferential_mem_simplePole X p.2 g⟩
    _ = 0 := finsum_curveLogResidue_eq_zero X g

end
end Hartshorne
